These are words you use when writing about workplace dynamics.
producing a good result;  very productive
Example: Seeing how they contribute within the team environment can prove to be a fruitful endeavor.
an activity that has a specified quality or result
Example: Observing individual members of your team over a period of time can prove to be a fruitful exercise.
accepted, done, or happening often or over a large area at a particular time
Example: Is there a prevalent team role that many of the team members share or are there particular roles missing from the group?
to influence the development of something
Example: This group of individuals is believed to be the people who shape, implement, and complete projects while driving a project from start to completion.
interested in a particular thing or activity
Example: Categories include action-oriented team members.
You can express reasons in a variety of ways using linking words and phrases.

You can also use -ing clauses to express the relationship between two or more reasons.
A clause is a part of a sentence. You may find two or more clauses in a sentence.

For example:
We lined up for hours hoping to get his autograph!
main clause: We lined up for hours
-ing clause: hoping to get his autograph!

If the -ing clause is placed at the beginning, a comma is needed between the clauses.
Example: Feeling tired, I left the office early.

When one action takes place before another, we use having + past participle.
Example:
Having passed my real estate exam, I thought I could start my own company.
When you want to explain something or why somebody does something, you can use an -ing clause . Usually the -ing clause is placed first.
Example: Not having a car, she couldn't attend church.

Take a look at some other examples from the text:
By observing individual members of your team over a period of time, you can understand each person's strengths.
When having a team with varied strengths, management can expect a reduction of potential behavioral tensions.
By understanding each role within a particular group, a person is able to develop their strengths in a group environment.
Report Verbs with Impersonal Passive Construction
When you want to report a fact or belief, you can use a variety of ways to construct your ideas. When you do not want to mention the source of the information, you can use a passive structure.
You can use the structure subject + passive verb + to-infinitive.

For example:
It is believed to be the easiest move.
If necessary, you can express the agent.

For example:
It is believed by the managers to be the quickest fix.
This group of individuals is believed to be the people  who shape, implement and complete projects while driving a project from start to completion.

images.text:
Employing a cohesive group of individuals to work in a team is often said to be difficult. In fact, it is believed to be one of the most difficult challenges facing management.
Wanting to focus on a person's education and skills, hiring managers often fail to consider behavior and personality traits when balancing a team. By understanding each role within a particular group, a person is able to develop their strengths and manage their weaknesses in a group environment. Teams can become unbalanced if all team members have similar styles of behavior or team roles. When having a team with varied strengths and experiences, management can expect greater cooperation and reduction of potential behavioral tensions. Roles can be broken down into three categories.  Categories include action-oriented team members.

This group of individuals is believed to be the people  who shape, implement and complete projects while driving a project from start to completion. Secondly, there are team-oriented roles such as coordinators, team-workers and resource investigators that provide support, assist in team cohesion and explore available options.
Finally, there are thought-oriented roles that focus on new ideas and approaches, evaluate ideas and provide specialist knowledge. If you are thinking about developing a team before a project starts or want to further yourself as a team player, consider what your colleagues bring to the table. Observing individual members of your team over a period of time, and seeing how they contribute within the team environment can prove to be a fruitful exercise.  After observing the team, keep a log or list of key strengths and traits that each team member has.

Looking at the list, compare each person's strengths and weaknesses. Think about which roles
and strengths you are lacking from your team. For example, is there a particular quality or strength shared by most of the team members, or is there a vital characteristic missing? Finding the right balance in staff is believed to be one of the most important factors in effective workplaces.
Why is a variety of team roles important?
